data.name: Hadad
data.long_meaning: In Arabic and Islamic tradition, Hadad is the name of the god of thunder and rain. He is often depicted as a powerful deity, capable of both destruction and creation. According to Islamic belief, Hadad is a sign of Allah's power and mercy, as he brings life-giving rain to the desert.

in_arabic.name: حداد
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من حديد، يعني الشخص القوي والشديد
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم حداد مشتق من كلمة حديد، وهي تعني الحديد أو الشخص الذي يعمل بالحديد. يوحي الاسم بالقوة والصلابة والشخصية القوية. في القرآن الكريم، يأتي ذكر الحديد في سورة الحديد، مما يعزز دلالة الاسم على القوة والمتانة. تاريخياً، كان اسم حداد يطلق على الأشخاص الذين يعملون في الحرف الحديدية، مما يجعله اسماً ذا أهمية حرفية ومهنية في المجتمع العربي.

in_urdu.name: حداد
in_urdu.meaning: حداد کا مطلب ہے قوی، سخت، اور مضبوط
in_urdu.long_meaning: حداد نام عربی زبان کے لفظ 'حديد' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے لوہا یا وہ شخص جو لوہے کے ساتھ کام کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام قوت، صلابت، اور مضبوط شخصیت کی دلالت کرتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کی روایات میں، یہ نام اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ قوت اور برتری کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हद्दाद
in_hindi.meaning: हद्दाद का अर्थ है मजबूत, कठोर और शक्तिशाली
in_hindi.long_meaning: हद्दाद नाम अरबी भाषा के शब्द 'حديد' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है लोहा या वह व्यक्ति जो लोहे के साथ काम करता है। यह नाम शक्ति, कठोरता और मजबूत व्यक्तित्व की ओर संकेत करता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम महत्व रखता है क्योंकि यह शक्ति और प्रभुत्व का प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: حداد
in_pashto.meaning: حداد د قوي، سخته او مضبوط سړي نوم دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: حداد نوم د عربي کلمې 'حديد' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې د اوسپنې يا هغه چا څخه چې د اوسپنې سره کار کوي، مانا لري. دا نوم د قوت، سختي او مضبوط شخصیت دلالت کوي. د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ارزښتونو په رڼا کې، دا نوم د يو قوي او متين کس په توګه تعبیر شوی دی.

in_english.name: Hadad
in_english.meaning: Means strong, hard, and powerful in Arabic
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hadad is derived from the Arabic root 'ḥ-d-d' which means iron or strong. It signifies strength, resilience, and a robust personality. In Islamic tradition, the name is associated with positive attributes such as fortitude and determination. Historically, it was also used to refer to blacksmiths or those working with iron, adding a layer of occupational significance. Across Muslim cultures, the name Hadad is valued for its connotations of power and endurance.

data.cultural_impact: In pre-Islamic Arabian culture, Hadad was a significant deity revered by many tribes. He was believed to control the elements of thunder and rain and was often invoked during times of drought or in times of war to ask for his protection and blessings. The name "Hadad" is still present in many Arabic names and places, reflecting the deep cultural roots of this ancient god.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Hadad is not considered a separate god but a manifestation of Allah's power. He is a reminder of Allah's control over the natural elements, and a testament to His ability to bring life from destruction. Hadad is also seen as a symbol of Allah's mercy and compassion, as he brings sustenance to the earth in the form of rain. This interpretation emphasizes the unity of godhead and reinforces the Islamic belief in one God.

historical_references.reference: Hadad was the name of a god worshipped in ancient Semitic cultures, including the Phoenicians, Canaanites, and Ammonites. He was the god of the storm, thunder, lightning, and fortunes of war.
historical_references.context: Pre-Islamic period, before the advent of Islam, Hadad was a prominent deity in the religious pantheon of ancient Semitic cultures.

historical_references.reference: After the advent of Islam, Hadad came to be identified with Al-Lat, a goddess revered among the Arabs, and was merged into the Islamic conception of Allah as a powerful deity overseeing thunder and rain.
historical_references.context: During the early Islamic period, Hadad was syncretized with Al-Lat and became a part of Islamic belief as a manifestation of Allah's power over natural phenomena.

modern_usage.modern_context: Hadad, also spelled Hadadabal or Hadadan, is a significant figure in Islamic mythology, revered as the God of thunder, rain, and fertility. Although not mentioned in the Quran, Hadad is a popular deity in pre-Islamic Arabian culture and is mentioned in various Islamic literature, poetry, and folk tales. In modern contexts, Hadad has gained popularity in various mediums such as video games, anime and manga, and literature and poetry. In video games like Final Fantasy and Assassin's Creed, Hadad is depicted as a powerful god with the ability to summon thunderstorms and control rain. In anime and manga, Hadad is often portrayed as a central character or inspiration, such as in the popular manga series 'Naruto' and 'One Piece'. In literature and poetry, Hadad is celebrated for his role in agriculture and the natural world, and is a recurring theme in Middle Eastern poetry and folklore.
